chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Ibn Mahbub, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: A man said in his presence: 'Allah is the Greatest,' so he (AS) asked him: 'Allah is greater than what?' The man answered: 'Greater than everything,' so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have defined/delimited it (by comparing it to something else),' the man asked: 'How should I say it?' He (AS) said: 'Say: Allah is greater than that which can be described.'

key_terms.أَنْ يُوصَفَ: That which can be described (attributed with qualities)
key_terms.حَدَّدْتَهُ: You have defined/delimited it (implying limitation by comparison)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct theological meaning of 'Allahu Akbar' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the man’s comparative definition of 'greater than everything' as a form of *takyif* (limiting God by analogy), instead prescribing 'greater than that which can be described' to affirm *tanzih* (absolute transcendence). This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on God’s incomparability, distinguishing between relative greatness and absolute, ineffable majesty that defies human conceptualization.
